title: Organise, Allocate and Monitor Availability and Productive Use of Resources

lessons.title: Planning resource needs for the week
lessons.html:
Planning resource needs for the week

This practical module is about the foreman's everyday job of making sure the right people, equipment and materials are in the right block at the right time, and are used productively.

Start from the operations plan

Each week, list the operations planned for each block from the production calendar and the manager's instructions: for example, shoot thinning in block 4, spraying in blocks 1 to 3, irrigation repairs in block 7. For each operation, work out:

  • Labour: how many workers, with which skills, for how many days.
  • Machinery: tractors, sprayers, trailers, platforms, mowers.
  • Equipment and tools: secateurs, ladders, bags, PPE, measuring tools.
  • Materials: chemicals, fertiliser, ties, wire, irrigation spares, fuel.

Use standard rates

Use known work rates from your records, such as trees thinned per worker per day or hectares sprayed per tractor per day, to estimate how many resources each job needs. For example, if a block has 8 000 trees and a worker thins about 200 trees a day, the job needs 40 worker-days - for instance 10 workers for 4 days.

Check availability

Compare what is needed with what is available. Check the leave list, the machine service schedule, stock levels in the stores, and other sections' needs for shared machines. Identify gaps early.

Resolve gaps

  • Reschedule less urgent work.
  • Move workers between teams.
  • Order materials or request extra labour from the manager.
  • Arrange repairs or borrow equipment.

Write the week's plan on a simple schedule showing block, operation, team, machines and materials per day, and share it with team leaders.

lessons.title: Allocating resources and issuing inputs
lessons.html:
Allocating resources and issuing inputs

Allocating people

Match workers to tasks using a skills matrix. Put trained, licensed operators on tractors and sprayers, and certified workers on chemical mixing. Balance teams so each has experienced workers and learners. Brief team leaders on targets and quality standards each morning.

Allocating machinery

Allocate each machine to an operator and job for the day. The operator does the pre-use check and logs hours and fuel. Avoid moving machines unnecessarily between distant blocks - group work by area where possible.

Issuing materials

  1. Prepare a job card or spray instruction showing block, product, rate, area and total quantity.
  2. The storekeeper issues exactly that quantity and records it.
  3. The operator signs for it.
  4. After the job, unused material is returned and recorded.

This links every kilogram or litre to a block and job, which supports cost control and audits. Agricultural remedies must be handled and stored according to their labels and Act 36 of 1947.

Tools and PPE

Issue tools and PPE against a register at the start of the day and check them back in. Replace worn PPE; workers must not do chemical work without the required PPE.

Transport

Plan worker transport so teams arrive on time. Workers must be transported safely: seated, not on trailers with loads, and in vehicles that are roadworthy.

Communicating changes

Plans change with weather and breakdowns. When you change allocations, tell team leaders, operators and the storekeeper straight away so that nobody waits or works on the wrong block. A quick message to a team WhatsApp group can help, but confirm important instructions face to face.

lessons.title: Monitoring use and reporting
lessons.html:
Monitoring use and reporting

Monitoring during the day

Visit each work site. Check that teams started on time, have what they need, are working to standard and are on track for the day's target. Look for idle time - workers waiting for bins, tractors standing, people walking long distances - and fix the cause.

Daily records

RecordInformation
Job cardBlock, operation, workers, hours, output
Machine logOperator, hours, fuel, faults
Store issues and returnsProduct, quantity, block, job
AttendancePresent, absent, late
Quality checksSamples checked, problems found

Measuring productivity

Calculate output per worker-day or per machine-hour and compare with the standard rate and previous days. For example, if the target is 200 trees per worker per day and a team averages 150, find out why: difficult trees, a training gap, late start, poor tools or low motivation.

Stock reconciliation

Each week, reconcile store stock: opening stock plus deliveries minus issues should equal closing stock. Investigate differences. Check expiry dates and reorder levels.

Reporting

Report weekly to the manager on:

  • Work completed against plan per block.
  • Labour hours and productivity.
  • Machine hours, fuel use and breakdowns.
  • Inputs used against plan and stock levels.
  • Problems and proposed solutions.

Keep reports short, factual and on time.

Improving

Use the information to improve next week's plan: adjust standard rates, change team compositions or schedule maintenance before peak periods.

Key points

  • Plan labour, machinery, tools and materials from the operations list using standard rates.
  • Check availability early and resolve gaps before the work starts.
  • Issue inputs against job cards and record returns.
  • Monitor idle time and productivity on site.
  • Reconcile stock weekly and report against plan.
